correctness.rationale: The gradient of f_p(x)=product_i(x_i/sqrt(p_i))^p_i is f_p(x)(p_i/x_i)_i. For V={a·x=0} with a mixed-sign normal, everywhere orthogonality along V∩S_p is sum_i a_i p_i/x_i=0. Positive homogeneity extends the identity to all positive x in V. With y_i=a_i x_i (a_i>0) and z_j=-a_j x_j (a_j<0), equal masses and equal reciprocal sums must hold for all positive redistributions; a sum c_r/t+c_s/(C-t) is not constant for any two positive coefficients. Hence exactly one positive and one negative a_i, and a_i²p_i=a_j²p_j gives the weighted pair seam. Converse by direct gradient evaluation, yielding exactly binomial(d,2). Tested representative d=2..9 gradient identities and nonpair reciprocal obstructions; analytic simplex argument proves all d and weights.
